PullRequest.Title: sessions: let any Customizations section register a badge
PullRequest.Body:

## Context

Customizations sections can signal that they need attention with a dot badge. Until now only contributed sections could declare one, and the only badge (Extensions, for suggested extensions) was hard-coded into the Agents window's Customizations button, sidebar link and collapsed sidebar header.

This refactor lets any section, built-in or contributed, register a badge, and makes every entry point read badges generically. It doesn't add badges to any new sections, and nothing changes visually.

## Changes

- **Section registry**: new `registerBadge(section, getBadge, supportsHarness?)` / `getBadge(section, harnessId)`, independent of widget creation. I removed the `getBadge` field from contributed sections so there is a single mechanism. Section visibility (harness `hiddenSections`, contribution support, `enablementSettings`) moves into `isVisible` / `isEnabled`, which the editor now reuses.
- **`aiCustomizationSectionBadges.ts`** (new):
  - `observeVisibleSectionsBadge` returns the description of the first visible section with a badge.
  - `observeVisibleSectionBadge` does the same for one section.
  - A badge is only read while its section is visible, since reading the Extensions badge logs an experiment trigger.
- **Editor**: `registerSectionBadges` reads badges for all sections from the registry.
- **Customizations button** (`ChatCustomizationsActionViewItem`): takes the combined badge description instead of an extension-suggestions boolean. The dot shows for migrations or any badge, and the tooltip and hover use the badge text. Migration text still takes precedence.
- **Agents window**:
  - The Extensions section registers its badge through a shared `getExtensionSuggestionsSectionBadge`.
  - Sidebar links show the badge of their own section.
  - The collapsed sidebar header shows the combined badge.
  - `showsExtensionSuggestions` is removed.
  - The Customizations row in the sessions list shows the combined badge through `CustomizationsNavigationState`.
- `AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` documents the badge contract.

## Notes for reviewers

- The button's tooltip now uses the badge description: "Customizations, Some installed extensions can be enabled in the Agents window." It used to say "Customizations (Extension Suggestions Available)".
- The registry has no change event, so a badge registered after an entry point renders appears only after the harness changes. All current registrations happen at module load.

## How to test

- Unit tests: `aiCustomizationSectionBadges.test.ts` (visible-section filtering, and hidden badges are never read), plus updated editor, hover and toolbar tests.
- Component Explorer: `sessions/aiCustomizationShortcutsWidget/WithExtensionSuggestions`, `CollapsedWithExtensionSuggestions` and `chat/aiCustomizations/aiCustomizationManagementEditor/SessionsContributedSectionBadge` render as before. The dot appears on Extensions, on the collapsed header, and on the editor's Extensions item.
- Manually: in the Agents window, with `extensions.experimental.agentsWindowManagement` enabled and extension suggestions available, the Customizations button, the Extensions sidebar link, and the collapsed Customizations header each show a dot.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint <changed files>`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationSectionBadges.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/chatCustomizationsHover.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/agentsWindowExtensionSuggestions.test.ts`: 156 passing

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Agents/Sessions Customizations sidebar, including expanded section links and the collapsed header badge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous UI rendering creates one observer for the collapsed header and one narrowly selected observer per rendered section link; badge text then updates a class, aria-label, and hover. No subprocess, filesystem, database, or network work blocks rendering. The extension provider reaches an existing shared derived extension-suggestion calculation and at most a deduplicated telemetry call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Log the extension-suggestions experiment trigger through telemetry when qualifying suggestions exist
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one telemetry event per treatment per telemetry service/window because logExperimentTrigger deduplicates with loggedTreatments; all UI observers share the same showBadge derivation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sidebar links and collapsed header directly observed IAgentsWindowExtensionSuggestionsService.showBadge, reaching the same extension scan and telemetry trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous logging call is reached while resolving the badge, but it is bounded and was already reached by the sidebar/header entry points before this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The sessions workspace exposes 11 management sections, but only registered badge providers are instantiated; production currently registers one Extensions provider. Per-section links select only their own section, while the combined header scans the bounded management-section list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All observer evaluation and DOM updates are serialized on the UI thread. The existing showBadge derived observable coalesces the installed-extension scan across all subscribers; there is no async fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider wrappers are resolved once per active harness within each observer. The underlying showBadge derivation caches the extension scan until extension/configuration/dismissal dependencies change; telemetry is negatively/positively deduplicated once per treatment per window.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed observer construction, owner disposal, section cardinality, shared derived caching, and telemetry deduplication were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future sections may register additional providers, but the current product registration count is one and the management-section list is statically bounded. No evidence shows expensive future providers or hot configuration churn.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff generalizes existing badge observation without duplicating the expensive extension scan, and all added synchronous work is small and lifecycle-bound.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Customizations navigation row in the Sessions list and react to badge, migration, harness, or configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CustomizationsNavigationState computes the first visible badge, then the list renderer updates one icon/hover/accessibility label. Badge evaluation is gated by the navigation entry's enabled observable. No filesystem, subprocess, database, or remote request is added to this row's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially emit the existing extension-suggestions experiment telemetry trigger while evaluating the Extensions badge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per treatment per telemetry service/window, independent of session count and list row count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: CustomizationsNavigationState directly read extensionSuggestionsService.showBadge on the same enabled path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Badge evaluation occurs before the row can display its indicator, but the telemetry event is deduplicated and the underlying extension computation is shared.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Customizations navigation row, with visibility checked against 11 static management sections and one production badge provider; cost does not scale with the number of sessions displayed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous derived-observable chain on the UI thread; list rendering does not start parallel operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared showBadge observable retains its computed value until relevant extension/configuration/dismissal state changes. The visible-badge array uses structural equality to suppress downstream updates when badge values are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the state-to-renderer path and its previous direct showBadge dependency were both inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration changes can invalidate visibility checks, but they produce only a bounded section scan and no per-session work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed generic state preserves one-row, cached behavior and does not add scaling boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the AI Customizations management editor and update section badges as harness visibility, settings, or badge state changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the sidebar registers one visible-badges autorun. It checks the static management-section list, maps current badges, and only re-splices the section list when an individual badge value actually changes. Harness/configuration changes also already rebuild visible sections elsewhere in the editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially log the pre-existing extension-suggestions experiment trigger when the visible Extensions section badge is observed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per treatment per window; one current production provider, regardless of editor section count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor previously invoked the contributed section's getBadge provider and observed the same showBadge value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May occur during initial badge resolution, but is bounded, deduplicated, and was already reached through the contributed Extensions section badge before the refactor.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: 10 management sections in the normal workbench and 11 in the sessions workspace; current production badge-provider cardinality is one. Badge updates iterate the bounded section list and DOM/list re-render is guarded by equality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is synchronous and serialized. No remote discovery, filesystem access, IPC, or subprocess is started by badge registration or observation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Badge observables are resolved once per active harness and reuse provider-level derived caches. Structural equality suppresses unchanged visible-badge arrays; section badge updates avoid list splice when the value is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registry cardinality, current registrations, editor update guards, and observable ownership were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A future large number of expensive badge providers could increase evaluation cost, but neither an unbounded registry population nor such providers exists in this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The generic built-in/contributed badge support adds bounded map/visibility work and preserves the existing provider boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render Customizations action buttons in the session bar, global toolbar, sidebar entry point, or chat input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each actually rendered action view item observes the first visible badge and updates one CSS class and tooltip/hover. Up to the four registered menu locations can create view items, but only active rendered locations subscribe. No filesystem, subprocess, database, or remote call is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially emit the existing, deduplicated experiment telemetry event while resolving the extension badge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per treatment per telemetry service/window across all action items because telemetry deduplication is global to the service and the underlying showBadge derivation is shared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each action item previously received and observed the same extensionSuggestionsService.showBadge observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Badge text is needed for the action indicator/tooltip, but no repeated network fan-out occurs per menu location.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most four registered menu locations, with active visibility controlled by context keys; each combined observer scans 10–11 static section IDs but resolves only the one registered production provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread updates; action items do not launch async work and share the provider's cached source observable.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The extension suggestion result is shared and cached. Each action item owns its wrapper/listener and disposal removes the configuration event subscription when the view item is destroyed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: menu registration cardinality, action item creation, shared source, and disposal paths were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneously visible toolbar locations varies by layout, but remains a small fixed bound.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Generic badge strings replace booleans without increasing expensive boundary cardinality or creating unbounded retained observers.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and relevant transitive paths. Checked synchronous UI work, observer/listener lifecycle, repeated badge evaluation, extension-list scan sharing, and telemetry boundary fan-out. The diff keeps expensive work cached and bounded, introduces no new I/O/IPC/subprocess/network fan-out, and has no high-confidence actionable performance regression.
